facts.why: 1940 is right for the carnival summer, but the card invites guests to dinner at Windsor Plantation, and in summer 1940 the house is an abandoned ruin Noah only dreams of fixing. He rebuilds it after the war, and Allie comes to dinner there when they meet again 'for the first time in seven years', which puts the house dinner around 1947. The stamp and the venue point at two different summers.

notes: Note 'It wasn't over. It still isn't over.' is Young Noah's line on Wikiquote. '365 letters', 'If you're a bird, I'm a bird', the Ferris wheel 'Will you go out with me?', the street scene and Walt Whitman all confirmed on Wikiquote. 'My Dearest Allie' is how Noah's last letter opens on Wikiquote; calling it letter 365 is a fair stretch, not flagged. If the 1940 stamp is kept, the Coca-Cola note 'Summer in Seabrook, 1940.' and the RSVP '1940' are fine as the carnival summer; change them only if the sign moves to 1947.

vibe.verdict: A cream invite from Windsor Plantation with lowcountry food and the street, the bird and the Ferris wheel feels right, but '365 letters' prints five times and the rowboat and rain kiss are missing.
missing: The rowboat among the swans, then the rain and 'Why didn't you write me?' (the lake)
'What do you want?' Noah asks Allie over and over (the fight at the house)
Allie paints again in the house Noah built
'I'll Be Seeing You', their song, as the old couple dance (title only, no lyrics)
Allie's mother hands over the letters she hid
ideas: Swap the crab cakes line 'Noah wrote her 365 letters' for 'The swans come in on the lake' so the rowboat scene is on the board
Swap the place card 'TABLE 365' for 'TABLE FOR TWO, BY THE LAKE' to cut one of the five 365s
Swap the footer 'Also on the list: 365 letters, one a day for a year' for 'Also on the list: the swans and the rain on the lake'
Swap the tagline 'He wrote to her every day for a year.' for the film's real tagline 'Behind every great love is a great story.'
